goldens.comment: In GroupPermissionsV2.canManage(), the permission fallback checks for both VIEW and MANAGE scopes (hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)), but canManage() should only grant access for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This means users with only VIEW permission on groups can pass the canManage() check, granting them write access they should not have. The canView() method correctly checks both VIEW and MANAGE, but canManage() should only check MANAGE.

In getGroupIdsWithViewPermission, hasPermission is called with groupResource.getId() and the same groupResource.getId() is added to granted, but hasPermission resolves resources by name (treating the argument as a group id) and the GroupPermissionEvaluator contract says this method returns group IDs that are later used as UserModel.GROUPS and in getUsersCount group filters. This mismatch means per-group VIEW_MEMBERS/MANAGE_MEMBERS permissions may not yield the expected group IDs for filtering and counts, and evaluation may effectively only look at the type-level 'all-groups' resource; consider revisiting whether this should operate on the underlying group ids (resource names) instead so it aligns with the JPA queries and the interface contract.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims there's an issue at line 250 of AdminPermissionsSchema.java, but the diff shows this file ends well before line 250. The diff adds GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE and related scopes to the schema, and adds a resolveGroup method. The finding suggests existing FGAP v2 realms won't receive the new Groups resource, but this is speculative about migration behavior not shown in the diff. The diff shows schema definition changes, not migration logic. There's no evidence in the diff of a migration problem - the schema is simply being extended with new resource types.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — A realm-wide Groups view grant also satisfies canManage(), allowing a read-only principal to create groups.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 65-72, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true. This means having VIEW permission on groups would satisfy canManage(), which is incorrect - VIEW should only allow reading, not creating/modifying groups. Compare this to canView() at lines 51-57 which correctly checks for VIEW or MANAGE, but canManage() should only check for MANAGE scope, not VIEW. This is a security bug where read-only permissions could allow write operations.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:168 — V2 inherits the legacy group-management contract even though its live methods only throw UnsupportedOperationException.

adjudication.rationale: The finding claims V2 inherits a 'legacy group-management contract' with methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException. Looking at the diff, GroupPermissionsV2 extends GroupPermissions and overrides several methods with actual implementations (canView, canManage, canViewMembers, canManageMembers, canManageMembership, getGroupIdsWithViewPermission). The methods that throw UnsupportedOperationException (isPermissionsEnabled, setPermissionsEnabled, viewMembersPermission, etc.) are intentionally unsupported in V2 as indicated by the 'Not supported in V2' messages - this is a deliberate design choice, not a defect. The class properly implements the GroupPermissionEvaluator interface through its parent class while intentionally disabling legacy permission management methods.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:70 — A realm-wide Groups `view` grant satisfies `requireManage`, allowing group creation without manage authority.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at GroupPermissionsV2.java lines 65-72, the canManage() method returns true if hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE) returns true. This means having VIEW permission on groups would satisfy canManage(), which is used for group creation (as seen in GroupsResource where groups are created). The finding correctly identifies that a VIEW grant would allow manage operations like group creation, which is a permission escalation bug. The canManage() should only check for MANAGE scope, not VIEW.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/permissions/GroupPermissionsV2.java:122 — The group permission scan passes authorization resource IDs as group names, so member-view grants are not recognized for user-list restrictions.

adjudication.rationale: Looking at line 122 in GroupPermissionsV2.java, the code is `if (hasPermission(groupResource.getId(), AdminPermissionsSchema.VIEW_MEMBERS, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE_MEMBERS))`. The finding claims 'authorization resource IDs as group names' are being passed incorrectly. However, examining the hasPermission method (lines 131-162), it takes a groupId parameter and uses `resourceStore.findByName(server, groupId)` to look up the resource. The resource names in the schema are set to the group ID (see resolveGroup in AdminPermissionsSchema.java which returns `group.getId()`). So passing `groupResource.getId()` is correct - the resource ID equals the group ID which is used as the resource name. The finding misunderstands the resource naming convention.

adjudication_records.issue_text: tests/base/src/test/java/org/keycloak/tests/admin/authz/fgap/GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java:275 — The view-only all-groups test never attempts a mutating group endpoint, so read-only grants can authorize writes without detection

adjudication.rationale: The finding points to testViewGroups() test at line 275 which only tests that VIEW permission allows listing groups. The test creates a VIEW-only permission but never attempts to call mutating endpoints (update, delete, add subgroup) to verify that VIEW permission correctly denies write operations. This is a valid test coverage gap - the test should verify that view-only permissions don't accidentally grant write access, especially given the permission system changes in this diff. However, this is not a bug in the production code itself, but rather incomplete test coverage for the new permission logic.

adjudication_records.issue_text: services/src/main/java/org/keycloak/services/resources/admin/UsersResource.java:395 — No integration test covers user counts with only group-member scopes, so the new group-ID filtering can leak or miscount users undetected

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows significant changes to user counting logic in UsersResource.java (lines 395-429), where `getGroupsWithViewPermission()` is renamed to `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` and the filtering logic is modified. The new test file `GroupResourceTypeEvaluationTest.java` tests group permissions including VIEW_MEMBERS and MANAGE_MEMBERS scopes, but focuses on user search operations (`users().search()`), not on the `getUsersCount()` endpoint. The finding correctly identifies that the count-specific code paths with the new group-ID filtering (lines 397, 422, 425, 429) lack dedicated test coverage. This is a legitimate test coverage gap for newly modified logic.
